title: rafkit: autocatalytic (RAF) sets in catalytic reaction networks
description: Maximal RAFs, strictly autocatalytic RAFs, irreducible-RAF sampling and census, exploitability, uninhibited RAFs (u-RAFs), and Gillespie simulation of catalytic reaction networks. Binary-polymer generators: Kauffman's K-BPM with optional cleavage and generated inhibition; Serra & Villani's C-BPM, where catalysis follows active-site complementarity rather than a coin flip; a templated ensemble in which nothing is drawn, where a species catalyses a ligation exactly when it contains the complement of the product or of the residues spanning the junction, shipped with the nulls a structured chemistry is compared against (degree-preserving and motif-matched shuffles, and the K-BPM and C-BPM at the same catalysis level); and the firing-disk construction, which grows a chemistry closed under its own production instead of enumerating one. Four modules are deliberately off that theme, each because it is a modelling choice that changes the answer: dilution reproduces the closed-form serial-dilution and CSTR conditions of Matsubara et al.; permeation implements size-selective membrane transport as a concentration difference rather than a count difference; thermo supplies bond energies and the rate constants they force, making catalysis a ratio applied to both directions so that detailed balance holds by construction rather than by assumption; and autocatalysis decides the thermodynamic consistency of autocatalytic cycles after Kosc et al. (PNAS 2025), which gives the library an external pass/fail anchor. Hand-computed known-answer tests throughout, regression tests against CatReNet's own output on a committed fixture, and worked examples reproducing published results. Reads and writes the CRS interchange format, exports PNML for the Petri net ecosystem, and exports ANDL with mass-action rate constants so a network runs unchanged in Spike, an independently developed stochastic simulator, with the semantics calibrated against Spike by measurement.
